title: Huronian glaciation (Gowganda Formation, Ontario)
summary: Glacial rocks of the Huronian Supergroup crop out along the north shore of Lake Huron in Ontario. The Gowganda Formation, one of three glacial events preserved in the supergroup, is the thickest and most commonly preserved, and geologists read its boulder conglomerate as a tillite laid down in an ice age.

uncertainty.note: The University of Waterloo museum gives the Gowganda conglomerate an age range of 2,200 to 2,450 million years; the range is the source stated span, not an error bar. The glacial event itself is not dated more tightly on any opened page.

where.modern_name: Cobalt, Timiskaming District, Ontario, Canada (Huronian glacial rocks crop out along the north shore of Lake Huron)
where.historical_name: Southern margin of the Canadian Shield, Ontario (no human geography)

importance.justification: A Paleoproterozoic glacial succession in Ontario, preserved in the thickest and best-known Huronian glacial unit.
